key_insight: A reduced-basis hybrid ML framework combining TBNN and UDE can learn frame-invariant viscoelastic constitutive laws from shear data and generalize to more complex flow types.
engineering_relevance: This enables more data-efficient digital twins and CFD-ready rheology models for predicting viscoelastic flow behavior in engineering devices such as contractions and cross-slot mixers.
method: Train on synthetic oscillatory-shear datasets generated from established viscoelastic models.
Embed a UDE constitutive law inside an open-source finite-volume solver for runtime stress evaluation.
Use a reduced tensor basis to improve physical consistency and simulation stability.
evidence_signal: The models were evaluated out of distribution in extensional, 2D, and 3D benchmark flows, including 4:1 sudden contraction and cross-slot cases, with accuracy improving when first normal stress difference data were added.
watch_item: Performance degrades as extrapolation increases, so shear-only training can miss quantitative fidelity in strongly extensional regimes and may fail near higher Deborah numbers.
paper_title: Harnessing Machine Learning for Hybrid Constitutive Modelling of Viscoelastic Fluid Flows in Computational Rheology
